newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: U.N. rejects military solution for Afghanistan.
newsitem.headline: U.N. rejects military solution for Afghanistan.

text.p: The senior United Nations peace negotiator in Afghanistan said on Tuesday a military solution to the Afghan conflict would risk changing the war from a domestic issue to one of international dimensions.

"If there is something you could call a military solution, it may just change the dimension of the political problem from a domestic issue to an international issue," Norbert Holl, head of the U.N. Special Mission to Afghanistan, told reporters in Kabul.
A recent BBC report quoted the leader of the purist Islamic Taleban as saying they were not interested in a negotiated solution to the conflict and would fight to the finish.
The Taleban captured the Afghan capital Kabul last September and now control over three quarters of Afghanistan.
The United Nations has been trying to negotiate an end to the fighting in Afghanistan since before the fall of the communist government in 1992.
The Taleban Information Minister said on Tuesday the United Nations had so far achieved little, but the Taleban would continueto cooperate with Holl's mission.
"We cannot say yet that the United Nations have failed 100 percent, but we can say that there has been no decisive result," Information Minister Amir Khan Mutaqi told Reuters.
Mutaqi rejected accusations that Taleban inflexibility was partly to blame for the failure of peace talks.
"For three years after the fall of the communists we were calling for negotiations, but there was no response from the other groups," Mutaqi said.
"We came to the conclusion that they were not willing to solve the problems via talks so we decided to clear them out of Afghanistan.
"Criticism of the Taleban is not justified," Mutaqi said.
Holl said that he would continue his mission to bring a negotiated end to the Afghan conflict.
"It is the position of the United Nations that a military solution to the Afghan problem is not possible. This is the clear policy of the United Nations whatever happens on the ground," he said.
